blocks.html:
This method searches an index for documents matching the given query. The
Search Module resolves the index's provider and delegates the query to it.

The free-text query is passed as `q` among the `filters`.

types.name: query
types.description: The query to run against the search index.

children.name: entity
children.description:
The name of the index to query, which defaults to the index whose name
equals the entity.

children.name: fields
children.description:
The dotted paths of the fields the search engine should return. Only fields
available in the search engine can be passed here.

children.name: filters
children.description: The filters to apply, including the free-text query as `q`.

children.name: $and
children.description: Filters that must all match.

children.name: $or
children.description: Filters of which at least one must match.

children.name: $not
children.description: Filters that must not match.

children.name: q
children.description:
The free-text query. Sits among the filters so a `query.graph` call converts
to `query.search` unchanged; the module lifts it out before compiling the
rest, so a provider never sees `q` as a field.

children.name: pagination
children.description: How the results are paginated and sorted.

children.name: skip
children.description:
The number of documents to skip before the returned hits. Mutually exclusive
with `cursor`.

children.name: take
children.description: The maximum number of hits to return.

children.name: order
children.description:
The fields to sort the hits by, keyed by the field's dotted path. The
reserved `_score` key sorts by relevance.

children.name: cursor
children.description:
An opaque provider cursor, as returned in a previous result's
`metadata.next_cursor`. Mutually exclusive with `skip`.

children.name: search_options
children.description: The options changing how the query is matched, scored, and aggregated.

children.name: attributes_to_search_on
children.description:
The dotted paths of the fields to match the free-text query against. Defaults
to every field marked `searchable` on the index.

children.name: match_strategy
children.description:
How query terms combine.

- `"all"` (default): every term must appear as a complete token.
- `"any"`: at least one term must match.
- `"last"`: typeahead. Completed terms must match in full; the last term
  is a prefix, so `"my sear"` matches `"My search results"`.

children.name: typo_tolerance
children.description: Whether to match terms that are misspelled by a character or two.

children.name: facets
children.description:
The facets to compute alongside the hits. A string is shorthand for a `value`
facet on that field.

children.name: disjunctive_facets
children.description:
Compute each facet ignoring the filter on that same field, so a storefront
keeps showing sibling values of an active filter. Needs one query per facet
on every engine reviewed, so the module expands them and hands the set to
`provider.searchMany`.

children.name: highlight
children.description: How the matched terms are highlighted in the returned hits.

children.name: distinct
children.description: Return at most one hit per distinct value of this field.

children.name: min_score
children.description: Discard hits scoring below this threshold.

children.name: include_score
children.description: Whether to return each hit's relevance score.

children.name: locales
children.description:
Query-time language hint, e.g. `["en"]`. Engines that analyze per language
(Meilisearch, Algolia) use it to pick the analyzer; a provider that cannot
honour it rejects it rather than silently matching differently. Defaults to
the index' `settings.locales`.

children.name: vector
children.description:
The options of a vector, or semantic, search to run instead of, or alongside,
the free-text query.

children.name: count
children.description:
How the total number of matching documents is computed. `"exact"` may be
rejected or slow depending on the provider.

children.name: provider_options
children.description:
Escape hatch for engine features the interface does not model, keyed by
provider identifier, e.g. `{ typesense: { drop_tokens_threshold: 0 } }`.

types.name: Promise
types.description:
The matching hits, any requested facets,
and the result's metadata.

blocks.html:
This method runs multiple search queries in a single call. Use it to run
queries against different indexes, or the same index with different filters,
without paying for a round trip per query.

Disjunctive facets are expanded here, then every query targeting the same
provider is handed to that provider's `searchMany` so the engine can pack
them into one request. Prefer `query.search` from application code, which
hydrates the hits through graph.

The options of a vector, or semantic, search to run instead of, or alongside,

children.name: count
children.description:

blocks.html:
This method adds documents to an index, replacing any document that already
exists under the same ID.

Prefer keeping an index up to date through its definition's `events` and
`consume` functions. Use this method for documents that no event describes,
such as data coming from a third-party system.

The returned task isn't waited on. A provider that applies writes lazily
leaves the task's status as `enqueued`, and it's the caller's choice whether
reading its own write back matters enough to wait for the task.

types.name: input
types.description: The documents to write.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index to write to.

children.name: documents
children.description:
The documents to write. Each
document must have an `id` property holding the index's primary key.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The write's task.

children.name: id
children.description:
The ID identifying the write in the search engine, which is passed back to
the provider's `waitForTask` method. It's set only for a deferred write,
since a provider applying writes inline has nothing to identify.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index the write was applied to.

children.name: status
children.description: The write's status.

children.name: error
children.description: The error that made the write fail, if its `status` is `failed`.

children.name: message
children.description: The error's message.

children.name: code
children.description: The error's code, as reported by the search engine.

blocks.html:
This method removes every document in an index matching the specified filters.

Deleting by ID isn't a special case: it's a filter on the index's primary
key, such as `{ id: ["prod_1"] }`.

types.name: input
types.description: The documents to remove.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index to delete from.

children.name: filters
children.description:
The filters selecting the documents to
remove. At least one filter is required.

children.name: $and
children.description: Filters that must all match.

children.name: $or
children.description: Filters of which at least one must match.

children.name: $not
children.description: Filters that must not match.

children.name: q
children.description:
The free-text query. Sits among the filters so a `query.graph` call converts
to `query.search` unchanged; the module lifts it out before compiling the
rest, so a provider never sees `q` as a field.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The write's task.

children.name: id
children.description:
The ID identifying the write in the search engine, which is passed back to
the provider's `waitForTask` method. It's set only for a deferred write,
since a provider applying writes inline has nothing to identify.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index the write was applied to.

children.name: status
children.description: The write's status.

children.name: error
children.description: The error that made the write fail, if its `status` is `failed`.

children.name: message
children.description: The error's message.

children.name: code
children.description: The error's code, as reported by the search engine.

blocks.html:
This method applies an event to every index that declared it in its
definition's `events`, using each index's `consume` function to turn the
event into document writes or deletions.

The Search Module subscribes to the declared events and calls this method for
you. You only need to call it directly to replay an event, or to ingest an
event that wasn't emitted through the Event Bus Module.

The returned promise resolves once the search engine has accepted the
writes. Failures are thrown, leaving redelivery to the event bus.

types.name: event
types.description: The event to apply.

children.name: name
children.description: The event's name.

children.name: metadata
children.description: Additional meadata to pass with the event.

children.name: eventGroupId
children.description:
The ID of the event's group. Grouped events are useful when you have distributed transactions
where you need to explicitly group, release and clear events upon lifecycle events of a transaction.

When set, you must release the grouped events using the Event Module's `releaseGroupedEvents` method to emit the events.

children.name: created_at
children.description: The date the event was emitted.

children.name: published_at
children.description: The date the event was published to the event bus. If it's a grouped event, this will be the date the group was released.

children.name: data
children.description: The data payload that subscribers receive. For example, the ID or IDs of the created user. (e.g. { id: "123" } or { ids: ["123", "456"] })

types.name: Promise
types.description:
One task per write. An event that no index
declared resolves to an empty array.

children.name: id
children.description:
The ID identifying the write in the search engine, which is passed back to
the provider's `waitForTask` method. It's set only for a deferred write,
since a provider applying writes inline has nothing to identify.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index the write was applied to.

children.name: status
children.description: The write's status.

children.name: error
children.description: The error that made the write fail, if its `status` is `failed`.

children.name: message
children.description: The error's message.

children.name: code
children.description: The error's code, as reported by the search engine.

blocks.html:
This method retrieves the registered indexes, their status, and the leaf
fields each of them stores. Definitions that haven't been migrated yet are
included with a `pending` status.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The registered indexes.

children.name: name
children.description: Unique index name, as used in `query.search({ entity })`.

children.name: entity
children.description: The `query.graph` entrypoint used to hydrate non-indexed fields.

children.name: provider
children.description: Identifier of the provider backing this index.

children.name: status
children.description: Lifecycle status of the index.

children.name: fields
children.description: Leaf fields stored in the index.

children.name: name
children.description: Dotted path of the field in the index, e.g. `title` or `variants.sku`.

children.name: type
children.description: The field's index type.

children.name: searchable
children.description: Whether the field is used for free-text matching.

children.name: filterable
children.description: Whether the field can be used in filters.

children.name: sortable
children.description: Whether results can be sorted by this field.

children.name: facetable
children.description: Whether the field can be faceted.

blocks.html:
This method retrieves the field paths an index can return. `query.search`
uses it to split the fields a caller asked for between the search engine and
`query.graph`.

types.name: index
types.description: The name of the index.

types.name: string[]
types.description:
The retrievable field paths, such as `title` or
`variants.sku`.

blocks.html:
This method retrieves an index's definition with the module's defaults
applied: the provider it resolved to, the physical index behind it, and the
`primary_key` its documents are keyed by, which is what a hit's `id` holds.

types.name: index
types.description: The name of the index.

types.name: name
types.description:
The index's unique name, which is what `query.search({ entity })` resolves
against.

types.name: entity
types.description: The `query.graph` entrypoint used to hydrate non-indexed fields.

types.name: fields
types.description: The fields the index holds, keyed by their path in the document.

children.name: type
children.description: The field's type.

children.name: array
children.description: Whether the field holds an array of the declared `type`.

children.name: searchable
children.description:
Whether the field is matched against a free-text query, optionally with a
`weight` boosting its relevance. The weight is applied at build time on some
engines, such as Meilisearch and Algolia, and at query time on others, such
as Typesense and Elasticsearch.

children.name: filterable
children.description: Whether the field can be used in a query's filters.

children.name: sortable
children.description: Whether results can be sorted by the field.

children.name: facetable
children.description:
Whether the field can be faceted, and which facet types it supports.
Defaults to `["value"]`, or `["range"]` for numeric and date fields.
`"stats"` is opt-in, since implying it would make numeric fields unusable on
providers without aggregations.

children.name: retrievable
children.description:
Whether the field comes back on hits. `false` for index-only fields, such as a
blob used purely for matching. `query.search` reads this to decide which
requested fields the engine can serve and which need `query.graph`.

Vector fields default to not retrievable — embeddings are not useful on
hits. Set `retrievable: true`, or `.retrievable()` in the DSL, to return
them.

children.name: fields
children.description: The fields of a nested object, only used when `type` is `object`.

children.name: type
children.description: The field's type.

children.name: array
children.description: Whether the field holds an array of the declared `type`.

children.name: searchable
children.description:
Whether the field is matched against a free-text query, optionally with a
`weight` boosting its relevance. The weight is applied at build time on some
engines, such as Meilisearch and Algolia, and at query time on others, such
as Typesense and Elasticsearch.

children.name: filterable
children.description: Whether the field can be used in a query's filters.

children.name: sortable
children.description: Whether results can be sorted by the field.

children.name: facetable
children.description:
Whether the field can be faceted, and which facet types it supports.
Defaults to `["value"]`, or `["range"]` for numeric and date fields.
`"stats"` is opt-in, since implying it would make numeric fields unusable on
providers without aggregations.

children.name: retrievable
children.description:
Whether the field comes back on hits. `false` for index-only fields, such as a
blob used purely for matching. `query.search` reads this to decide which
requested fields the engine can serve and which need `query.graph`.

Vector fields default to not retrievable — embeddings are not useful on
hits. Set `retrievable: true`, or `.retrievable()` in the DSL, to return
them.

children.name: fields
children.description: The fields of a nested object, only used when `type` is `object`.

children.name: dimensions
children.description:
The dimensionality of the embedding stored in a `type: "vector"` field.
Required for vector fields; meaningless on any other type. When `embed` is
omitted, every vector written to the field must have exactly this many
components.

children.name: embed
children.description:
When `true` on a vector field, documents pass a string and the engine
embeds it at write time, and for `search_options.vector.query` at query
time. Omit `embed` to supply embeddings yourself as a `number[]`.

children.name: provider_options
children.description:
Field options specific to a search engine, keyed by provider identifier, such
as `{ meilisearch: { ... } }`.

children.name: dimensions
children.description:
The dimensionality of the embedding stored in a `type: "vector"` field.
Required for vector fields; meaningless on any other type. When `embed` is
omitted, every vector written to the field must have exactly this many
components.

children.name: embed
children.description:
When `true` on a vector field, documents pass a string and the engine
embeds it at write time, and for `search_options.vector.query` at query
time. Omit `embed` to supply embeddings yourself as a `number[]`.

children.name: provider_options
children.description:
Field options specific to a search engine, keyed by provider identifier, such
as `{ meilisearch: { ... } }`.

types.name: events
types.description: Events related and that can affect the data for this index.

types.name: consume
types.description: Executed on event ingestion to determine the action that needs to be performed on the index.

types.name: seed
types.description:
Yields the index's documents in batches. Ran when there is no data in the
index or on reindex.

types.name: primary_key
types.description: The field whose value keys the index's documents.

types.name: provider
types.description: The identifier of the provider backing this index.

types.name: settings
types.description: The settings applied to the index.

children.name: synonyms
children.description: Terms treated as equivalent when matching, keyed by the term they expand to.

children.name: stop_words
children.description: Terms ignored when matching, such as `the` or `a`.

children.name: typo_tolerance
children.description: How misspelled terms are matched.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Whether typo tolerance is enabled at all.

children.name: min_word_size_for_one_typo
children.description: The shortest term length that tolerates a single typo.

children.name: min_word_size_for_two_typos
children.description: The shortest term length that tolerates two typos.

children.name: disabled_on_attributes
children.description: The dotted paths of the fields that must always match exactly.

children.name: faceting
children.description: The defaults applied to the facets computed on this index.

children.name: max_values_per_facet
children.description: The maximum number of values returned for a facet.

children.name: sort_by
children.description: Whether facet values are ordered by their count or alphabetically.

children.name: pagination
children.description: The limits applied when paginating this index.

children.name: max_total_hits
children.description: The maximum number of hits a query can page through.

children.name: distinct_attribute
children.description:
The dotted path of a field that hits are deduplicated by, returning at most
one hit per distinct value.

children.name: locales
children.description: The languages the index's text is analyzed for, such as `["en"]`.

children.name: provider_options
children.description: Index settings specific to a search engine, keyed by provider identifier.

types.name: definition_hash
types.description:
A hash of the definition, which the module compares to detect that an index
drifted from its definition and must be migrated.

types.name: physical_name
types.description:
The concrete index the provider reads and writes. Differs from `name` under
an index prefix, or while a `swap` builds into a replacement.

blocks.html:
This method triggers a background job that rebuilds one or more indexes from
their definitions' `seed` functions. Medusa handles reindexing automatically, as explained
in the [Reindexing and Migrations Guide](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/infrastructure-modules/search/reindexing).
This method is useful to trigger the reindex manually after changing what a `seed`
produces, or to recover an index whose documents drifted from their source
of truth.

The job is started, not awaited: the returned result only tells you which
indexes are being rebuilt.

types.name: input
types.description:
The reindex options, such as which
indexes to rebuild and what strategy to use. If not provided, every index is
rebuilt with the `swap` strategy.

children.name: index
children.description:
The name of the index, or the names of the indexes, to rebuild. If not
provided, every registered index is rebuilt.

children.name: strategy
children.description: The strategy to rebuild the index with.

children.name: filters
children.description:
Filters passed to the index definition's `seed` function to rebuild only a
subset of the index's documents.

types.name: Promise
types.description:
The ID of the job performing the
reindex, and the indexes it rebuilds.

children.name: job_id
children.description: The ID of the background job performing the reindex.

children.name: indexes
children.description: The names of the indexes being rebuilt.

blocks.html:
This method plans what it would take to bring the physical indexes in line
with the loaded index definitions. Planning is separate from executing it. It's
useful for printing the actions, or executing them later with [executeIndexMigrationPlan](/references/types/SearchTypes/interfaces/types.SearchTypes.ISearchModuleService#executeindexmigrationplan).

types.name: Promise
types.description:
The actions required to
bring the physical indexes in line with the definitions. Indexes that are
already up to date are returned as `noop` actions.

children.name: action
children.description:
The index does not exist yet. Nothing is serving it, so it is built
directly under its live name and filled in place.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index to create.

children.name: physical_name
children.description: The physical index to create it under.

children.name: definition_hash
children.description: A hash of the definition the index is created from.

children.name: live_physical_name
children.description: The index serving reads now.

children.name: live_definition_hash
children.description: A hash of the definition the index currently serving reads was built from.

children.name: provider
children.description: The provider the definition now binds to.

children.name: previous_provider
children.description:
The provider that currently holds this index. Set only when it differs
from `provider`, so execute can drop the previous engine's data.

blocks.html:
This method executes a migration plan, creating and altering physical
indexes. Every action is idempotent, so executing the same plan twice is a
no-op.

The indexes this method creates are filled by the seed that runs at
application start, so an index it creates serves nothing until then.

```ts
const actions = await searchModuleService.createIndexMigrationPlan()
await searchModuleService.executeIndexMigrationPlan(actions)
```

types.name: actions
types.description:
The actions to execute, as
returned by [createIndexMigrationPlan](/references/types/SearchTypes/interfaces/types.SearchTypes.ISearchModuleService#createindexmigrationplan).

children.name: action
children.description:
The index does not exist yet. Nothing is serving it, so it is built
directly under its live name and filled in place.

children.name: index
children.description: The name of the index to create.

children.name: physical_name
children.description: The physical index to create it under.

children.name: definition_hash
children.description: A hash of the definition the index is created from.

children.name: live_physical_name
children.description: The index serving reads now.

children.name: live_definition_hash
children.description: A hash of the definition the index currently serving reads was built from.

children.name: provider
children.description: The provider the definition now binds to.

children.name: previous_provider
children.description:
The provider that currently holds this index. Set only when it differs
from `provider`, so execute can drop the previous engine's data.

types.name: Promise
types.description:
Resolves when the physical indexes are created and
altered.
